review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Family groups versus kinship relations, household units, shared family-role genera, full and half siblings, and great-grandparent/great-grandchild roles. Correct co-role pairs misrepresented as converses.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Cambridge, Collins, Gramota and ONS support selected corrections. Definitions are not copied; scope and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. A family group, a kinship relationship and a person in a family role are different kinds of concept. Role definitions use the same reference person; changing that reference does not license a genus. No new blanket exclusions are introduced.

sense_decisions.scope: The gender-neutral family role covering brothers and sisters, distinct from a particular sibling pair or kinship relation. Do not require the reference person to have an opposite-gender sibling.
A parent of the reference person's parent; a person in a family role, not the relation or a mandatory male/female pair.
A child of the reference person's child. The role does not require the person to be a minor.
A person's partner in marriage. Use a gender-neutral genus for existing husband and wife; do not import generic partner, an eligibility rule or a particular jurisdiction.
The family role covering the reference person's aunt or uncle, including the relevant parent-sibling and marriage-connected uses. It does not require both an aunt and an uncle.
The family role covering the reference person's niece or nephew. No age restriction or opposite-gender counterpart is asserted.
A person related through biological descent. This person role is distinct from blood kinship as a relation; no coefficient of relatedness is asserted.

Select the two-parent-and-children family unit. Correct the dictionary gloss that incorrectly includes grandparents. No requirement about parent gender, a child's age, marriage or a shared address is imported.
A family group extending beyond the parent/child unit to other relatives. Co-residence and blood-only membership are not required; the group is not a kind of nuclear family.
A family unit consisting of one parent and that parent's child or children. This is the unit's composition, not a claim that no other biological parent exists or a legal family classification.

A domestic living unit comprising one person or multiple people with shared living arrangements. It need not be a family and is not a house building or the household-economy discipline. Use the collection genus so one-person units are allowed.
A household with one resident member. The living unit is distinct from the individual person; census eligibility rules are not imported.
A household with more than one resident member. Members need not be related.
The restricted case in which the whole household is one co-resident family group. It has both household and family genera; not every household is a family and not every family shares a household.
A sibling sharing both biological parents with the same reference person. This scope is not an assertion about the completeness or value of a family.
A sibling sharing one biological parent, while the other is different, relative to the same person. Do not import a step-sibling synonym.
A brother sharing both biological parents with the reference person.
A sister sharing both biological parents with the reference person.
A brother sharing exactly one biological parent. Exclude the dictionary's stepbrother synonym and the ambiguous Russian svodny translation.
A sister sharing exactly one biological parent. Exclude the dictionary's stepsister synonym.
A half sibling sharing the biological mother, with a different biological father, relative to the same person.
A half sibling sharing the biological father, with a different biological mother, relative to the same person. Select the precise sibling sense, not every colloquial blood-relative usage.
A half brother on the shared-mother side.
A half brother on the shared-father side.
A half sister on the shared-mother side.
A half sister on the shared-father side.
A parent of the reference person's grandparent. Do not classify it as that same person's grandparent by changing the reference point.
The grandmother's or grandfather's mother, relative to the same reference person.
The grandmother's or grandfather's father, relative to the same reference person.
A child of the reference person's grandchild. Do not import the dictionary grandchild genus when it changes the reference person or generation.
The grandson's or granddaughter's son, relative to the same reference person.
The grandson's or granddaughter's daughter, relative to the same reference person.
Plural parents may be a duplicate or a collective; leave its genus unchanged until the choice is reviewed. Its false temporal sequence is removed.
Mother/mom duplicate and its potential references need a separate merge review.
The archaic mother form is an established word, not an automatically malformed term; defer deduplication.
Grandfather/older-man meanings need review before merging the ded record.
Family can also denote a taxonomic rank or group. Do not silently merge it into the human family record.
Marriage relationship, wedding event and marital formation remain distinct review topics.
The old husband/wife converse example needs a context-scope review; no new universal gender pairing is asserted.
Cousin may differ in gender and genealogical degree across English and Russian; defer its sense split.

review.limits: No legal status, eligibility, inheritance right, custody rule, DNA percentage or biological diagnostic claim. Household wording is a broad living-unit sense, not an import of every UK census criterion. Exact member counts and reference-person bindings are scope notes, not executable cardinality or genealogy rules. Mother/mom/mater and grandfather aliases, plural parents, family/taxonomic-family, spouse-context rules, wedding causation and cousin scope require separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Keep upper object/relation exclusion 7999; remove the incorrect family-to-social-relation genus that supplies its witness. No exclusion edge is changed or added.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Kinship, blood kinship, family, family roles and person/group anchors are reused; ambiguous historical duplicates remain queued.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
